items.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: a guy named Whitman Red, they called him. He was ne’er-do-well and a thief and a gambler and a pimp-type person

ctx.x: No. Josh White, the folk singer. He used to stop by all the time. But one time this man in the town we were living in at the time, which was Kenton, Ohio – a guy named Whitman Red, they called him. He was ne’er-do-well and a thief and a gambler and a pimp-type person – that kind of guy – shot and killed a man on the railroad tracks. It was a big thing, because it happened right outside our house. All the neighbors were just astounded by this murder that took place. The police were there. They were measuring…

Then they all left. My mother was washing the dishes. She looked out the window at the police still there, walking around. She must have forgotten that I was there, because she said, “Poor Red.” And I thought, poor Red? He’s the murderer. My mother had compassion for the murderer. I’ve since understood that that is a very high spiritual thing to do.
